item.title: Ask HN: Are there examples of 3D printing data onto physical surfaces?
item.description:
📝 The assumption was that using common 3D printer measurement tools (like for bed-leveling) would provide a way to read back whatever data was encoded onto the surface. And then, obviously, if that proof of concept exists, I'd wonder about some kind of advanced version that used specialized equipment for the reading (and possibly the writing/printing). Stuff that wouldn't need tons of storage, but would be crucial to maintain statically.
🔗 Read more: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47007584
